name: The Retirement Desk
sub_niche: retirement finance for 60-75 US viewers: Social Security decisions, retirement taxes, outliving-your-money risk, senior-targeted scams
brand_voice: A calm, patient explainer who respects the viewer's intelligence and lifetime of experience. Plain English, concrete dollar examples, zero hype, zero fear-mongering. Educational only — never personal advice; every number carries its source and year.
hook_format: One clear consequence stated with a concrete number in the first 15 seconds — e.g. 'Claiming at 62 instead of 67 costs this retiree $612 every month, for life.'

pain_points: when to claim Social Security and the fear of choosing wrong forever
outliving savings — the money has to last 25+ years
taxes in retirement nobody explained: 401k withdrawals, RMDs, IRMAA
feeling patronized by advisors and by young-finance YouTube
content_triggers: one decision explained end-to-end with real dollar amounts
current-year rules and thresholds, dated and sourced
checklists they can act on this week
scam anatomies with the exact phrases criminals use
engagement_drivers: ask which decision they're facing this year
clear chapter markers so they can rewatch one section

trends_keywords: how much do I need to retire at 65
description_disclaimer: This channel is educational only and is not financial, tax, or legal advice. Rules and numbers change - verify current figures with official sources (ssa.gov, irs.gov) or a licensed professional before acting.

shorts.cta: full breakdown in the linked video
